# v1.79: signal-truth — tip-verify as a status phase, alias-drift detection, legacy-bound sweep, decision event stream, line-anchored feedback, a model guard that can fail; version bump

Scoped 2026-07-24 under the operator mandate recorded in `.overseer/DECISIONS.md`,
ruling `.planning/rulings/2026-07-24-v179-signal-truth.md` — the binding design
contract for this version. One theme: every signal the harness sends — to the
operator's eyes, to their phone, or to its own retry loops — must be true, current,
and precise.

HEADLINE: in one day of live operation the operator personally caught two signals
lying. A watch pane rendered four green tasks and a full progress bar while tip-verify
had failed and a resume was quietly re-verifying — the surface hid the one fact that
mattered (OBS-146). And the claude `opus` alias re-pointed to a brand-new model
between two probes thirty minutes apart with zero events fired anywhere, leaving
tier, pricing, and learned-routing stamps describing a model the channel no longer
serves (OBS-145, captured live on Opus 5 release day). Meanwhile the wall-clock-bound
flake class red-flagged its third surface of the day (OBS-147, a legacy bound the
v1.78 controlled-time law predates), and the orca consultation identified the two
cheapest high-value signal upgrades: decision events an operator can receive off-desk,
and review feedback that names the exact line instead of gesturing in prose. Truth
rendering, truth detection, truth transport, truth addressing — one version.

FOLDED IN AFTER SCOPING (operator ruling, 2026-07-24, recorded in `.overseer/DECISIONS.md`):
T7 closes OBS-153. The probe session that ran between scoping and execution found four
defects of one class — matchers anchored flush-left meeting an interface that indents,
borders and hard-wraps its own output — and three were fixed on the base this spec now
sits on. The fourth fails OPEN: the model-confirmation guard returns success for ANY
model, including a deliberate mismatch, because it reads a banner the interface prints
inside a bordered panel. A guard that cannot fail is the purest violation of this
project's law that unparseable results are failures, and it is the one blocking
condition on the operator's deny-lift gate. It belongs to signal-truth by theme: a
signal that always says yes carries no information.

Why one chain: T4 (decision stream) shares the status surface files with T1
(tip-verify phase), so T4 depends on T1; T2, T3, T5, and T7 are disjoint lanes; T6 is
the version bump and depends on all six.

Authoring laws in force (standing style, carried from v1.71–v1.78 and the OBS ledger):
single-line goals, regex-clean criteria with no acceptance criterion naming a file
extension or version number literal, judge items single-clause and self-contained,
worker context[] files tracked in git, no complexity-4 task, and every task carrying a
typed test oracle lists a collectable test path in files[] up front. No task adds a
new test file under an existing tracked test directory — every oracle lands in an
existing test file named in files[]. The OBS-143 law holds: no new test asserts
across a real-time bound it does not control. No task changes the dependency set, so
the stack-coupling gate is not triggered; no module is added or deleted, so the
structure reference is untouched. Exit bar per task: full npm test suite green; npm
test stays zero-token throughout (fake adapters and stub binaries only, never a real
agent CLI — the drift check's identity probe runs only inside a real doctor
invocation and is stubbed in tests).

Non-goals (dispositions per the ruling): race mode / verified best-of-N (deferred to
a dedicated headline version — too wide to ride beside five small truth tasks);
OrcaDriver spike, quota-reset benching, adapter manifest, UI-evidence artifacts
(backlog per the orca synthesis); lifting the K2.7 deny or restoring the k3 pin
(both probes are now green, but the lift gate additionally requires T7 landed — the
decision returns to the operator afterwards and is never pre-applied here); any mobile
app, web service, database, or notification server (transport belongs to
herdr/bridges); any silent re-tier or routing change from drift detection (advisory
only); any change to verdict parsing semantics — anchored comments are an optional
extra that degrades to prose, never a new failure mode.

## T1: tip-verify renders as a first-class status phase

- goal: the status and watch surfaces render the tip-verify state explicitly — the failing gate named on failure, the re-verify attempt visible during a resume, and no progress presentation reading as terminal green while tip verification is failed or pending
- shape: implement
- deps: none
- files: src/cli/commands/status.ts, tests/cli/status.test.ts, tests/cli/status-watch.test.ts, tests/cli/status-liveness.test.ts
- context: src/run/journal.ts
- complexity: 2
- acceptance:
  - test: a journal whose last run-end carries a failed tip verification renders the failed gate by name in the status header
  - test: a resume in progress after a failed tip verification renders as a re-verification in progress rather than a completed run
  - test: the done-count presentation never reads as terminal success while tip verification is failed or pending
  - test: a run whose tip verification passed renders exactly as today
  - judge: the surface derives every rendered claim from journal events rather than inferring optimistic state

## T2: doctor detects resolved-identity drift on alias channels

- goal: doctor compares each alias-served channel's resolved model identity against the identity its tier and pricing stamps were dated for and warns to reclassify on drift, reading identity from the adapter's on-disk session store when available and a minimal stated-identity probe otherwise, without ever re-tiering or changing routing by itself
- shape: implement
- deps: none
- files: src/adapters/claude-code.ts, src/cli/commands/doctor.ts, tests/cli/doctor.test.ts, tests/adapters/claude-usage.test.ts
- context: src/adapters/types.ts, src/config/config.ts
- complexity: 3
- acceptance:
  - test: an alias whose resolved identity differs from its stamped identity produces a drift warning naming both identities and the reclassification policy
  - test: an alias whose resolved identity matches its stamp produces no warning
  - test: identity resolution prefers the zero-cost on-disk source and falls back to the probe only when the store is silent
  - test: a drift warning changes no tier, no channel availability, and no routing decision
  - judge: drift detection is advisory in the same sense as existing doctor warnings and cannot mutate configuration

## T3: legacy wall-clock bounds move onto controlled time

- goal: the liveness suite bound that flaked this release's tip verification and the approve and greenness-exit bounds fingerprinted in release verification move onto controlled time or load-proof margins so a loaded machine can no longer fail them
- shape: tests
- deps: none
- files: tests/run/daemon-interactive.test.ts, tests/cli/approve.test.ts, tests/cli/greenness-exit.test.ts
- context: tests/drivers/herdr.test.ts
- complexity: 2
- acceptance:
  - test: the liveness scenario that flaked release verification passes deterministically under an artificially slowed environment
  - test: no touched suite retains an assertion across a real-time bound it does not control
  - judge: each converted oracle still fails when the behavior it guards genuinely regresses

## T4: decision events stream machine-readable

- goal: the watch surface gains a machine-readable decision-event stream over the journal — stable events for phase changes, gate verdicts, escalations, required human decisions with the exact approval command and evidence pointer, and run end — plus an optional fire-and-forget webhook sink on the existing decision-tier notifications
- shape: implement
- deps: T1
- files: src/cli/commands/status.ts, src/drivers/types.ts, tests/cli/status-watch.test.ts, tests/cli/status-watch-purity.test.ts
- context: src/run/journal.ts, src/drivers/herdr.ts
- complexity: 2
- acceptance:
  - test: a required human decision emits one machine-readable event carrying the exact approval command and an evidence pointer
  - test: the stream replays identically from the same journal so a reconnecting consumer reaches the same state
  - test: a configured webhook sink receives decision-tier events and its failure never affects the run or the stream
  - judge: the stream is pure formatting over journal truth with no new state, service, or storage

## T5: verdicts carry line-anchored feedback

- goal: judge and review verdicts may carry optional line-anchored comments that retry and consult prompts render as an anchored review block, with a missing or malformed comment block degrading to today's prose behavior and never affecting the verdict itself
- shape: implement
- deps: none
- files: src/gates/llm.ts, src/gates/acceptance.ts, src/gates/review.ts, src/adapters/prompt.ts, tests/gates/acceptance.test.ts, tests/gates/review.test.ts, tests/gates/judge-retry.test.ts
- context: src/run/consult.ts
- complexity: 3
- acceptance:
  - test: a verdict carrying well-formed anchored comments renders them as an anchored review block in the retry prompt
  - test: a verdict with a malformed or absent comment block parses exactly as today with no new failure mode
  - test: anchored comments never alter the verdict outcome the gate records
  - judge: the retry prompt names each commented location precisely enough for a worker to act without searching

## T7: the model-confirmation guard stops failing open on a bordered banner

- goal: the interactive model confirmation reads the served model identity out of the banner as the interface actually renders it, reports a genuine mismatch as a failure, and reports an unrecognized printed name as unknown rather than as either success or mismatch
- shape: implement
- deps: none
- files: src/adapters/kimi.ts, tests/adapters/kimi-tui-seed.test.ts, tests/adapters/kimi-auth.test.ts
- context: src/adapters/prompt.ts, tests/fixtures/kimi-editor-readiness/frame-01.txt
- complexity: 3
- acceptance:
  - test: the model identity is extracted from a banner captured verbatim from the live interface, borders and indentation included
  - test: a banner naming a model other than the one assigned is reported as a mismatch
  - test: a banner whose printed model name has no known mapping to a channel identifier is reported as unknown rather than as a mismatch
  - test: the session identifier is extracted from that same captured banner
  - judge: the confirmation never reports success when the banner names a model other than the assigned one
  - judge: the banner used as the test fixture is a verbatim capture rather than hand-authored text

## T6: version bump

- goal: increment the package version for this release with a themed changelog entry and a current release-guide tag example
- shape: chore
- deps: T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T7
- files: package.json, package-lock.json, CHANGELOG.md, RELEASING.md, tests/cli/version.test.ts
- context: package.json, CHANGELOG.md
- complexity: 1
- acceptance:
  - test: the built CLI's version command reports the same version string as the package manifest
  - test: the package manifest, lockfile, and release guide all carry the current version — no stale prior-version declaration survives a bump
  - judge: the changelog entry names the signal-truth theme rather than generic filler
  - judge: the prior-release constant in the version parity test moved forward to the release before this one
